deck.title: General Physical & Chemical Properties of the First Row of Transition Elements, Titanium to Copper

front_blocks.md: Define **transition element**.

back_blocks.md: A **transition element** is a d-block element that forms one or more stable ions with an incomplete d subshell.

cards.back_md: A **transition element** is a d-block element that forms one or more stable ions with an incomplete d subshell.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Scandium is classified as a transition element.

back_blocks.md: **False.** Scandium is not a transition element because its only stable ion, Sc<sup>3+</sup>, has no electrons in the 3d subshell — giving it the electronic configuration of [Ar].

front_blocks.md: Why is zinc not classified as a transition element?

back_blocks.md: Zinc forms only one ion, Zn<sup>2+</sup>, which has a **complete** 3d subshell with the electronic configuration [Ar]3d<sup>10</sup>. Transition elements must form at least one ion with an **incomplete** d subshell.

back_blocks.md: The 3d<sub>xy</sub> orbital has **four** lobes that point **between** the x and y axes.

front_blocks.md: Define **3d****<sub>z</sub>****<sup>2</sup>**** orbital**.

back_blocks.md: A **3d**<sub>**z**</sub><sup>**2**</sup>** orbital** is a d orbital with two main lobes pointing along the z-axis and a doughnut-shaped ring of electron density around the centre.

cards.back_md: A **3d**<sub>**z**</sub><sup>**2**</sup>** orbital** is a d orbital with two main lobes pointing along the z-axis and a doughnut-shaped ring of electron density around the centre.

front_blocks.md: List four characteristic properties of transition elements.

back_blocks.md: Transition elements have: **variable oxidation states**, act as **catalysts**, form **complex ions** and form **coloured compounds**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Iron can form ions with oxidation states of +2 and +3.

back_blocks.md: **True.** Iron forms Fe<sup>2+</sup> (Fe(II)) and Fe<sup>3+</sup> (Fe(III)) ions, illustrating the variable oxidation states typical of transition elements.

back_blocks.md: Transition elements are found in the **d** block of the Periodic Table, between Groups **2** and **13**.

front_blocks.md: What are the common oxidation states of vanadium?

back_blocks.md: Vanadium commonly exhibits oxidation states of **+2, +3, +4 and +5**.

front_blocks.md: Why can transition elements have variable oxidation states?

back_blocks.md: The 3d and 4s subshells are **similar in energy**, so a similar amount of energy is needed to remove different numbers of electrons. This allows transition elements to form ions by losing varying numbers of electrons.

front_blocks.md: Define **autocatalysis**.

back_blocks.md: **Autocatalysis** is a process in which a reaction is catalysed by one of its own products as it forms, causing the reaction to speed up progressively.

cards.back_md: **Autocatalysis** is a process in which a reaction is catalysed by one of its own products as it forms, causing the reaction to speed up progressively.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When transition elements form ions, the 4s electrons are lost before the 3d electrons.

back_blocks.md: **True.** When transition elements form ions, the 4s subshell electrons are removed first, followed by electrons from the 3d subshell.

back_blocks.md: The most common oxidation state of transition metals is **+2**, formed when the **4s** electrons are lost.

front_blocks.md: Give the electronic configuration of Ti<sup>3+</sup>.

back_blocks.md: Ti<sup>3+</sup> has the configuration **1s**<sup>**2**</sup>** 2s**<sup>**2**</sup>** 2p**<sup>**6**</sup>** 3s**<sup>**2**</sup>** 3p**<sup>**6**</sup>** 3d**<sup>**1**</sup>. Two 4s electrons and one 3d electron are removed from the titanium atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Transition elements act as catalysts because they have vacant d orbitals that can accept lone pairs from ligands.

back_blocks.md: **True.** The energetically accessible vacant d orbitals allow ligands to donate lone pairs via dative bonds, enabling transition element ions to act as catalysts.

front_blocks.md: Define **complex ion**.

back_blocks.md: A **complex ion** is a charged species consisting of a central metal atom or ion surrounded by one or more ligands, which donate lone pairs to form dative covalent bonds.

cards.back_md: A **complex ion** is a charged species consisting of a central metal atom or ion surrounded by one or more ligands, which donate lone pairs to form dative covalent bonds.

front_blocks.md: Why do higher oxidation states become less stable towards the end of the 3d transition series?

back_blocks.md: As **nuclear charge** increases across the d block, the 3d electrons are attracted more strongly to the nucleus and become **harder to remove**. Higher oxidation states are therefore less stable and elements are more likely to retain their 3d electrons.

front_blocks.md: In a catalytic cycle, Fe<sup>2+</sup> acts as a reducing agent by losing an electron to form **..........** , which can then act as an **..........**  agent.

back_blocks.md: In a catalytic cycle, Fe<sup>2+</sup> acts as a reducing agent by losing an electron to form **Fe**<sup>**3+**</sup>, which can then act as an **oxidising** agent.
